newsitem.title: USA: Georgia adds 16,600 new jobs in June - labor chief.
newsitem.headline: Georgia adds 16,600 new jobs in June - labor chief.

text.p: Georgia added 16,600 new jobs in June, putting total nonfarm employment at 3.6 million, state Labor Commissioner David Poythress said.
More than half of the new jobs involved outdoor work, including gardening, landscaping, construction and lumber mill work and recreation-related work.

Sixty percent of the new jobs created, or 10,300, were in the metropolitan Atlanta area, Poythress said. Albany and Augusta added 700 new jobs while Columbus gained 600 and Macon added 500. Savannah lost 1,100 jobs and Athens lost 300 during the month.
Georgia has added 44,200 new jobs over the year, an increase of 1.2 percent, Poythress said.

The number of Georgians drawing unemployment benefits increased by 2,645 in June. Poythress said 43,479 people drew $19 million in benefits in June, compared with 40,834 people and $18.74 million in benefits in May.
